chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Steel guitar and T-Bone Walker's style
summary: Smith used a steel guitar; Durham says T-Bone Walker was early, with gimmicks, strong bass strings and a jazzy blues swing.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: How did he get that sort of Hawaiian effect? What did he do?
He had a steel guitar. He had a Hawaiian guitar.
Oh, he did?
Yeah, he played that on the ______.
I had one, too.
Yeah.
I had one, too. I had one, I used to play it.
Well, really, what T-Bone was doing was very early, wasn't it?
(Unintelligible.) That's the way I look at it today.
He was?
He was unready, when I heard him, what he was playing then. We didn't know to appreciate it. It's the same thing now today. He had guts and everything in it.
(Unintelligible) plays a couple of those passages here now.
Well, he --
And he could handle his bass strings,
(unintelligible) all down in there and everything.
Yeah. Yeah, and he also -- I mean, he's been with the other blues guitar players. He had sort of more of a jazz feeling, too.
Who's that, T-Bone?
Yeah.
Sure.
I mean, you know, --
A jazzy blues deal.
Swing like mad.
Blues swing, yeah.
Yeah.
He had a lot of gimmicks. Wasn't a matter of so many of them, but what he did was so effective.
(Unintelligible) kind of the creator of that style.
Yeah.
So far as I know. I didn't know anybody else before him.
